_comment: Prompts that belong to no skill's domain. Routing runs them against the
whole catalog, so they are the `unrelated` control group for every skill at
once -- which is why they live here instead of being copy-pasted into each
Only add a prompt here when nothing in the catalog is close to it. A prompt
that sits near one skill in particular belongs in THAT skill's dataset with
`"expect_skill": null`, where it is reported as that skill's near-miss and
its owner is the one who maintains it.
These are routing-only: behavior mode stages exactly one skill and these
belong to none, so they carry no `should` / `should_not` assertions.
A false trigger here is much more serious than a near-miss failure. It means
a description is broad enough to capture ordinary programming work.

cases.prompt: Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists, and add unit tests for it.
Write a Python function to reverse a linked list.
My pytest run fails with a Windows path error in test_utils.py. Track down the bug and fix it.
Add a GitHub Actions job that runs ruff on every pull request.
What is the capital of France?
